correctness.rationale: For each maximal allowed run of length L, g summands fill every block integer 0..g(g^L−1), i.e. length L+1 positions with exactly g−1 forbidden highest block values. Enlarged consecutive runs are digit-disjoint because between original runs at least one missing position. Finite prefix density is the product of independent block fractions and mandatory zero digits. If product zero, periodic-superset bounds yield density zero; if positive, all but finitely many gaps are length one and the forbidden future blocks have summable densities, so a tail union bound proves genuine natural density for arbitrary x. Removing zero summands excludes only O((log x)^{g−1}) low-block-sum values. For h<g, carries <=h−1 at every excluded input digit give arbitrarily many independent forbidden digit restrictions of density (h/g)^m. Explicit L_j=N+j² achieves positive density arbitrarily near 1. Independent exact tests checked 36 finite base/run examples, not a proof of infinite-density convergence.
residual_risks: No result for h>g, mixed-colour unions or representation counts; finite checker is not a density proof.
